findings.title: Upsampling cache can return stale or colliding eligibility results
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key containing only organization ID and hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). The defined invalidate_upsampling_cache helper is never called when the project allowlist option changes, so projects removed from the allowlist can continue to be overcounted and newly added projects can continue to be undercounted until expiry; a hash collision between different project sets would also reuse the wrong eligibility. The TTL can additionally expire between the multiple _get_event_stats calls made by the dashboard-split flow, producing inconsistent transformations within one request.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried
findings.body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset and executes the query against it, but is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the closure variable dataset. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with discover or another split_dataset that can differ from the original dataset, so an errors split query can be denied upsampling because the outer dataset was metrics/transactions-like, or upsampling can be considered based on a dataset different from the one that will run the query.

findings.title: Substring event.type check misclassifies discover queries in both directions
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query only searches request.GET['query'] for the substring 'event.type:error'. A negated query such as '!event.type:error' therefore returns True and applies sum(sample_weight) to non-error events, while valid error-focused forms such as '!event.type:transaction', 'event.type:[error,default]', or the errors-only split query constructed by the endpoint ('(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction') return False because the helper also ignores the actual query argument passed to _get_event_stats. This causes overcounting for excluded-error queries and missed upsampling for legitimate error queries.

findings.title: upsampled_count has no fallback for events without sample_weight
findings.body: The aggregate is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)), replacing a row count that counted every event. Any stored error row whose sample_weight is null or 0 (for example events ingested before client sampling was enabled/configured for an allowlisted project, or events without a client_sample_rate) contributes 0 instead of 1, so historical or unsampled buckets in the retention window can drop to zero or be undercounted after the transformation. The added tests only cover events explicitly given client_sample_rate through the new factory helper.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public Discover function
findings.body: The new SnQLFunction does not set private=True, unlike internal-only aggregates, so it becomes user-callable through the Discover query builder. A caller can submit upsampled_count() directly as a yAxis/field for projects and datasets that never passed the organization-events-stats allowlist and dataset checks, bypassing the gating in error_upsampling.py and receiving raw sum(sample_weight) results (including misleading zero values for transaction data).

findings.title: Accidental git submodule added to the repository root
findings.body: This new file adds 'Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a' as a submodule named sentry-repo at the repository root. It is unrelated to the upsampling feature and will change checkout/CI behavior for every developer by introducing a nested Sentry checkout; it should be removed before merging.
